content.title: About
content.content: Fatty fish are species that contain a high level of omega‑3 polyunsaturated fatty acids such as EPA and DHA. Examples include salmon, mackerel, herring, sardines and trout. They have a rich flavor, firm texture and are valued for their beneficial fats, protein, vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Omega‑3s from fatty fish support heart and brain health.
Wild salmon gets its pink color from a diet rich in crustaceans and krill.
Herring has been traditionally preserved by pickling, smoking and canning in northern cuisines.
Mackerel migrates long distances, traveling thousands of kilometers each year.
In Japan, saba (yellowtail) is traditionally eaten during New Year celebrations.

items.title: Rich source of omega‑3
items.content: EPA and DHA help maintain cardiovascular health, reduce inflammation and support brain development.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Fatty fish provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, B6 and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides selenium, iodine and potassium, essential for thyroid function and fluid balance.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: One of the few natural food sources of vitamin D, which supports bone health.

items.title: Mercury contamination
items.content: Some larger predatory fish may contain higher mercury levels; pregnant women and children should limit intake.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals with fish allergy can experience reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium in smoked products
items.content: Smoked or salted fish can be high in sodium, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: People with pancreatitis or gallstones may experience discomfort after eating fatty fish.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fatty fish can be baked, grilled, steamed or enjoyed as canned. It pairs well with lemon, herbs, olive oil and vegetables. For a lighter preparation, it can be marinated in yogurt or soy sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh fish in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen fish should be kept at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Use airtight packaging and keep away from strong odors.
